chapter: Recent years and early piano influences
title: Tatum's antenna fingers and counting the keyboard
summary: Fingers like antennae, whole-tone scale with thumb, and a ritual arpeggio to measure the keyboard.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: You see. And not only that, then he had... His technique was... I mean, he was partly blind, you know, and there's a certain amount of... With blind players, you have to have aa certain amount of feel, really. And I would say... A comparison is, like, a grasshopper has what do you call them...

Antenna-type. His fingers seemed to have a sort of antenna-type feeling for the key. Like, he would run an arpeggio from top to bottom, and he would trill a whole chord coming down, and then like in a whole-tone scale he would take...his thumb would... He would play with his thumb. He would roll his thumb over, say, the four white keys, and all in perfect alignment, you know. Of course, his thumbnail never... He never lost it, never wore it down! But he had a way of doing a whole tone scale, where naturally you only had three or five black keys... So, say, from B to F, the thumb will take care of that. Well, he would insert the B-flat, the three black keys along...and in perfect alignment...you know, in perfect...
And then the next two white keys, and then the other two white keys in perfect sequence. And then he could go on with his other line.

Now, when he sat at the piano, naturally, the first thing he did was get the presence of the keyboard, by running an arpeggio with his left hand, continuing with his right hand, and hitting the last note with his pinky -- POW! Then that way he had the keyboard...he had a dimensional... you know, he had the presence of the keyboard in his mind, where every note was...I mean, how far he could go. And if it was a small piano, he'd feel around and he'd say, "Well, no, this is not it."
In other words, he counted it out first.
But that pinky would hit that note with such power that sometimes I felt sorry for the piano! And that established his attitude towards what he was going to do with that instrument.
